Damage is the process by which a player or monster's [[life]] or [[energy shield]] is reduced.

This page focuses on damage being dealt by the player. For information on damage dealt by minions, see [[Minion]]. For information on how elemental damage affects the player, see [[status ailment]]s and [[resistance]]s. For information on when damage is applied see, [[receiving damage]].

==Damage calculation==
The basic damage calculation is:

: ''Damage = (Base_Damage + Added_Damage) * Increased_Damage * More_Damage * Hit_Rate * (Critical_Strike_Damage * Critical_Strike_Chance)''

* '''Base_Damage''': The primary damage of the skill.  This is either specified in the skill itself (and increases with the level of the skill gem), or is determined by the damage of your weapon (in the case of most Attacks).
* '''Added_Damage''': Additional flat damage applied, modified by the skill's [[damage effectiveness]] value.
* '''Increased_Damage''': Additional percentage damage applied. All applicable sources of increased damage stack additively (e.g. two +10% increased damage modifiers add together to make 20% increased damage: 100% + 10% + 10% = 120%).
* '''More_Damage''': Additional percentage damage applied.  All unique sources of more damage are multiplicative with each other (e.g. two +10% more damage modifiers will multiply on top of each other: 110% * 110% = 121%).
* '''Hit_Rate''': The rate at which the damage is applied, typically based on [[attack speed]] or [[cast speed]].
* '''Critical_Strike_Damage''': See [[Critical strike#Critical strike multiplier|Critical Strike Multiplier]].
* '''Critical_Strike_Chance''': See [[Critical strike#Critical strike chance|Critical Strike Chance]].

In general:, '''More Damage''' is usually more effective than '''Increased Damage''', due to diminishing returns from stacking increased damage modifiers, and the multiplicative nature of '''More Damage''' modifiers.

===Damage variance===
Damage variance describes the difference between the highest possible value that a source of damage can roll and the lowest possible value. Sources with higher differences are described as having higher damage variance, with lightning damage being characterized as having the highest damage variance of all damage types. For example, {{c|mod|Adds 190 to 220 Cold Damage}} is an example of a source with low damage variance, while {{c|mod|Adds 1 to 1000 Lightning Damage}} would be an example of a source with high damage variance. Mechanics like [[Luck|Damage is Lucky]] works favourably with skills with high damage variance.

The damage number rolled is rolled per hit, and not per skill use, unlike crits.

Some sources of damage are characterized by a lack of damage variance. For example, {{il|Bloodthirst Support}}'s {{c|mod|Supported Attacks deal Added Physical Damage with Weapons equal to 2% of Maximum Life while on Low Life}} is a static source of damage. This may be useful for players seeking to test in-game damage values while eliminating the uncertainty of damage rolls.

==Damage source==
All sources of damage are encompassed by one of four categories:<ref name="TalismanPoisonQA2" /> 
* [[Attack]] damage
* [[Spell]] damage
* [[Secondary]] damage
* [[Damage over time]]
A single hit or instance of damage can only be one of these four categories at a time and are mutually exclusive. Modifiers which apply specifically to one damage source never innately apply to any others, though some skill modifiers allow the numeric values of one damage source to be used in calculations for another (e.g. {{il|Vortex}} - note that in this example, the damage over time component is still not considered dealing spell damage, and will not be affected by modifiers to spell damage ''taken'', such as Unnerve). Generic modifiers (e.g. Elemental Damage or simply just "Damage") can affect multiple damage sources.

==Damage type==
A [[hit]] can be composed of several types of damage, but each damage type is calculated separately, including damage range rolls. Currently there are five types of damage:

* [[Physical damage]] - Considered the default damage type. Auto-attacks typically deal physical damage before conversion, and almost all weapons (and [[unarmed]]) have base physical damage. Physical [[damage over time]] can be inflicted with the [[Bleeding|bleed]] [[ailment]], or another common debuff, [[Corrupted Blood]].
* [[Fire damage]] - One of three elemental damage types. Dealing a [[Critical Strikes|critical strike]] with fire damage inflicts [[ignite]], however ignites also occur based on [[Ignite#Mechanics|chance to ignite]]. Fire damage over time from ignites, [[burning ground]], or other sources is classified as [[Burning|burning damage]].
* [[Cold damage]] - One of three elemental damage types. Hitting an enemy with cold damage can inflict the [[chill]] [[ailment]], while dealing a [[Critical Strikes|critical strike]] with cold damage can inflict [[freeze]]. Cold damage over time can be inflicted by certain spells, typically also applying [[Chill]].
* [[Lightning damage]] - One of three elemental damage types. Dealing a [[Critical Strikes|critical strike]] with lightning damage can inflict [[shock]]. Base lightning damage tends to have higher variability in damage ranges, with minimum and maximum damage values often being significantly further apart than similar fire or cold damage modifiers. Lightning damage over time is significantly less common than its counterparts, mostly limited to the ''Siphoning'' [[monster modifier]], [[Shock and Horror]]'s beam skill, [[The Shaper]]'s beam, and some environmental hazards.
* [[Chaos damage]] - Considered the rarest damage type, chaos damage bypasses [[Energy Shield|energy shield]] and damages life directly. Chaos damage has the benefit of not being [[reflect]]able. Chaos damage over time can be inflicted with the [[poison]] ailment. Many chaos skills also innately cause debuffs that deal chaos damage over time.

[[Darkness]] is a non-standard damage type only used by the '''Darkness''' debuff in [[Delve]]'s Azurite Mine, never by enemies (or players).<ref>https://www.pathofexile.com/forum/view-thread/3414849/filter-account-type/staff</ref> It can be mitigated by "darkness resistance" purchased at the [[Voltaxic Generator]], as well as by generic modifiers to damage taken.

==Keywords exclusive to damage sources== 
Some keywords are exclusive to a specific [[damage source]].

===Attack===
====Melee====
Melee damage is a category of damage exclusive to the [[Damage#Attack_Damage|attack damage source]]; in the case of damage instances who inherit keywords from a parent skill (such as [[ignite]] or [[Puncture]]'s bleed) the melee keyword is not inherited.

====Unarmed====
:''Main article: [[Unarmed]]''
Unarmed damage is a subcategory of Melee Damage and therefore inherits damage modifiers from the Melee and Attack keywords.

====Weapon-specific keywords====
Weapon-specific keywords are derivatives of the [[Damage#Attack_Damage|Attack damage source]] and therefore are not inherited by damage instances who inherit keywords from a parent skill (such as [[ignite]], [[puncture]]'s bleed, or [[Caustic Arrow]]'s caustic ground).

==Other keywords==
Beyond source and type, there are several other ways to classify damage which are best referred to by their generic name '''Keywords'''. In the case of a damage instance triggered by a parent skill (such as [[ignite]]), these modifiers are all inherited from the triggering hit. See [[keyword]]s for more information.

===Area===
Certain skills have an Area of Effect (''AoE'' for short) and can affect multiple enemies or allies at once.

===Elemental===
Elemental Damage modifiers affect all types of elemental damage (Fire, Cold and Lightning). Chaos damage is not considered elemental.

===Mine===
[[Mines]] are skills which are thrown (like Traps) and detonated by a separate command.

===Minion===
{{Redirect|Minion Damage|the support gem|Minion Damage Support}}

Modifiers to minion damage function as a [[Damage#Generic Modifiers|generic damage modifier]] granted to the minion. This means it will apply to all damage dealt regardless of [[Damage#Damage Sources|source]], [[Damage#Damage Types|type]], or keywords.

===Projectile===
Note that skills with the [[bow]] keyword are considered to implicitly be projectiles. 

===Totem===
Modifiers to totem damage function as a [[Damage#Generic Modifiers|generic damage modifier]] granted to the totem. This means it will apply to all damage dealt regardless of [[Damage#Damage Sources|source]], [[Damage#Damage Types|type]], or keywords.

===Trap===
Modifiers to trap damage function as a [[Damage#Generic Modifiers|generic damage modifier]] granted to the trap. This means it will apply to all damage dealt regardless of [[Damage#Damage Sources|source]], [[Damage#Damage Types|type]], or keywords.

===Generic modifiers===
Damage modifiers that have no restrictions or specifications are commonly referred to as ''generic damage modifiers''. These modifiers are potent since they will apply to all damage dealt by the modified skill regardless of [[Damage#Damage Sources|source]], [[Damage#Damage Types|type]], or keywords.

===Reflected damage===
:''Main article: [[Damage reflection]]''

===Damage reduction===
[[Armour|Damage reduction]] only affects physical damage. The other four damage types each have their own [[Resistances|resistance value]].

==Unique items==
===Applying to all damage types===
[[Unique items]] that modify damage for ''all'' [[damage type]]s [[global]]ly.

{{Drop enabled unique item table
|tables=item_stats
|join=items._pageID=item_stats._pageID
|where=item_stats.id="damage_+%"
|level=1
|stat_column1_header=+#% Damage
|stat_column1_format=%s%%
|stat_column1_stat_format=add
|stat_column1_stat1_id=damage_+%
}}

===Conditionally applying to all damage types===
Unique items that modify damage for ''all'' damage types globally based on a condition.

{{Drop enabled unique item table
|tables=item_stats
|join=items._pageID=item_stats._pageID
|where=
  (  
    item_stats.id != "damage_+%"
    AND item_stats.id LIKE "damage_+\%%" 
  )
  OR item_stats.id LIKE "%damage_vs%"
  OR item_stats.id LIKE "%damage_while%"
|level=1
|stat=1
}}

===Other unique items===
Unique items that otherwise interact with ''all'' damage types, but don't fit any of the above categories.

{{Drop enabled unique item table
|tables=item_stats
|join=items._pageID=item_stats._pageID
|where=
  item_stats.id NOT LIKE "damage_+\%%"
  AND item_stats.id NOT LIKE "damage_over_time_+\%%"
  AND item_stats.id NOT LIKE "damage_vs%"
  AND item_stats.id NOT LIKE "damage_while%"
  AND item_stats.id LIKE "damage_"
|level=1
|stat=1
}}

==Passive skills==
Certain passive skills and many [[Ascendancy class]] passives grant increased Damage under certain conditions.

{{Query passive skills
|where=
  passive_skill_stats.id LIKE "%damage_+\%%"
  AND passive_skill_stats.id NOT LIKE "%physical%damage%"
  AND passive_skill_stats.id NOT LIKE "%lightning_damage%"
  AND passive_skill_stats.id NOT LIKE "%cold_damage%"
  AND passive_skill_stats.id NOT LIKE "%fire_damage%"
  AND passive_skill_stats.id NOT LIKE "%chaos_damage%"
  AND passive_skill_stats.id NOT LIKE "%elemental%damage%"
  AND passive_skill_stats.id NOT LIKE "%mine_damage%"
  AND passive_skill_stats.id NOT LIKE "%trap_damage%"
  AND passive_skill_stats.id NOT LIKE "%minion_damage%"
  AND passive_skill_stats.id NOT LIKE "%totem_damage%"
  AND passive_skill_stats.id NOT LIKE "%attack%damage%"
  AND passive_skill_stats.id NOT LIKE "%area_damage%"
  AND passive_skill_stats.id NOT LIKE "%projectile_damage%"
  AND passive_skill_stats.id NOT LIKE "%damage_over_time%"
  AND passive_skill_stats.id NOT LIKE "%poison_damage%"
  AND passive_skill_stats.id NOT LIKE "%bleeding_damage%"
  AND passive_skill_stats.id NOT LIKE "%melee_damage%"
  AND passive_skill_stats.id NOT LIKE "%spell_damage%"
  AND passive_skill_stats.id NOT LIKE "%wand_damage%"
  AND passive_skill_stats.id NOT LIKE "%bow_damage%"
  AND passive_skill_stats.id NOT LIKE "%burn_damage%"
  AND passive_skill_stats.id NOT LIKE "%hand_damage%"
  AND passive_skill_stats.id NOT LIKE "%spectre_damage%"
  AND passive_skill_stats.id NOT IN ("damage_+%_with_two_handed_weapons")
}}
